text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A meeting of the aid-to-Pakistan consortium of donor countries in Paris has indicated that financial commitments will be forthcoming in support of a strong implementation of the economic revival programme recently announced by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government.
- The road between Dir distrtict in the North West Frontier Province and the provincial capital Peshawar was blocked on Wednesday by demonstrators protesting against shortages of wheat flour.
- Pakistan is among 23 countries carrying economic espionage in the United States, said a report based on intelligence gathered by the CIA and private security agencies.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Wednesday that Pakistan valued new Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's desire to resolve problems between the two countries and would respond very positively.
- The planned privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd in the near future has become highly doubtful in view of its declining profits and lack of buyers' interest.

- The government has constituted a six-member committee to review the agreements with the sponsors of all of about 90 private power projects, including the Hub Power, to reduce their expected adverse impact on balance of payments and on consumers.
- Hoechst Ravi Chemicals Ltd, a joint venture between Hoechst and Ravi Chemicals Group, has become operational, producing raw materials for the paint industry.
- The national budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) will be presented in parliament on June 14 with special emphasis on structural adjustments and economic stabilisation.
- Senior officials of Pakistan Navy on Wednesday strongly denied any wrongdoing in the Agosta 90-B submarine deal with France and said the submarine was selected on merit.

- Pakistan has conveyed its concern to the United States for allowing access to Indian naval officers and experts into the technology and operational capabilities of P-3 C Orion surveillance aircraft supplied to Pakistan after last year's relaxation of an arms embargo.
- Pakistan may not resist the extradition of Squadron Leader Qasim Bhatti of the Pakistan Air Force to the United States for his alleged involvement in heroin smuggling to that country.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, talking to reporters in Islamabad on Wednesday, called for a judicial inquiry into the crisis created by shortages of wheat flour and publish the findings.
- The State (Central) Bank of Pakistan has adjusted the rupee down to 40.24/40.44 to the dollar after shedding 12 paisa from 40.12/40.32 fixed on October 22.
- Pakistan is expected to launch a three-year dollar Eurobond next month after roadshows that will kick off on May 5, a syndicate official at lead manager ANZ Investment Bank said.
